_about: Notes: your inner voice on the slate (docs/master-design.md §5). First person, hedged, short. A thought has stages that change as you act; answering it writes its journal line and may raise the next question. Fills in {braces} come from the game.

stages.start: The lander recycles so well it'll keep me alive a long, long time, Castellanos says. It'll never hold a crew, though. The base is out there in the pallets.

air.journal: The lander looks after me. The pallets are for the base: that's what I'm out here for.

stages.start: Parachute on the ridge {dir} of the hatch. Pallet 1, life support. That's where the base starts.
stages.near: It's ours. A pallet in the dust by the canopy, latches still shut.
stages.open: Pallet's open: the module's air cartridge, the sample kit and ten ration packs. The cartridge can wait by the lander till the module comes.

parachute.journal: Found the first pallet under its parachute, right where the orbiter's photo said.

stages.start: The base came down on a dozen pallets, and the storm scattered the lot. Eleven still out there somewhere.

cargo.journal: Every pallet is home, or as home as they'll get.

stages.start: Castle wants me to watch it go down. Someone in training swore Martian sunsets are blue. I'd like to see one for myself.

sunset.journal: Watched the sun go down from outside. It really is blue round the sun, like cold glass. Nobody said how quiet it would be.

stages.carrying: The core's air cartridge. Twenty kilos, but it'll carry. It can wait by the lander till the core's down.
stages.staged: The module's air cartridge is waiting by the lander. It plugs into the module's outside socket.

module_air.journal: Plugged pallet 1's air cartridge into the module's socket. Its tank's full: room to breathe for more than one.

stages.start: ARDEN doesn't think the cabin battery lasts the night. There's a power pallet out there; find it before dark and the heater can run.
stages.night: Dark now. Heat or lights through the night: I don't think the battery gives me both. Warmth matters more.

stages.start: Long day. The landing seat reclines. I could sleep till dawn, or I could go and look at the stars.
That's the day. Back to {home} and sleep.
stages.late: Getting dark. Whatever's left will keep till tomorrow. Back to {home} and sleep.

stages.start: Cold in here. The heater's on the wall switch, if the battery can spare it.

cold.journal: Warm again. I'd forgotten how much I like my fingers.

stages.start: From up here I can see two more parachutes. One off to the {a}, one to the {b}. One at a time, though: the suit's air won't stretch to both and back.

chutes.journal: Two more parachutes from the ridge, and both pallets found.

stages.near: This pallet's flat and wide. The power kit, maybe.
stages.open: A rolled solar blanket and a battery pack: the module's power. It'll keep, packed, till the core's down.

power_pallet.journal: Laid pallet 2's solar blanket out at the module's socket. The module holds the night now.

stages.near: There's a cradle in this one the shape of GAR-Y. Please be in there.

stages.start: GAR-Y keeps turning towards the {dir}. A pallet beacon, maybe, too faint for my suit.
stages.near: Frost on the ground in this hollow, and a pallet sitting in it.

tools.journal: Pallet 3, in the frost hollow: a rock hammer, a headlamp and a patch kit. The headlamp throws a lot more light than the suit lamp.

sunset_gary.journal: Watched the sun go down with GAR-Y. Neither of us made a sound. It's the first time it's felt like we live here.

stages.start: GAR-Y's been out all night. It's marked frost in a hollow, something big and cold, and something metal. Hold G by it and it'll show me.

gary_scouted.journal: GAR-Y spent the night scouting while I slept. Frost, ice and iron, all of it within a morning's walk. So that's what it's for.

stages.start: I'm not alone out here.

not_alone.journal: Not alone out here after all. GAR-Y sticks so close it bumps my boots.

stages.start: Something is tapping on the hull outside the hatch. Something small, and patient.

tapping.journal: There was something tapping on the hull when I came round. It was GAR-Y.

stages.low: Cabin water's lower than I thought. A day and a bit, maybe, so I'd better find ice to melt.{where}
stages.empty: The tank's dry, and I can't go long without a drink. Ice, melted in the lander's bench melter.

water.journal: Melted my first ice in the lander's melter. It came out cloudy and tasted of rust and nothing. Best drink I've ever had.

stages.seen: Dark red rock studded with little grey balls. Haematite, I think. Iron. Nothing to smelt it with yet.

iron.journal: Haematite beads from the outcrop: iron, once I've got a way to smelt it.

stages.seen: A wall of buried ice, showing through the dust in slabs. Tonnes of it. I can only chip a few kilos by hand.

ice_wall.journal: The ice wall is old snow, layer on layer. Enough water for years, if I could dig it properly.

stages.start: The storm left good parts in this junk. The lander's little printer could make something useful of them.

salvage.journal: Printed GAR-Y a sled hitch from storm junk. Small, but mine.

stages.start: Should get a picture of this for the journal. The slate has a camera.

photo.journal: Took a picture for the journal.

stages.start: My slate's lit up on the console. Something from orbit.
The suit beeped. Its wrist pad shows how much air I've got left. I should keep an eye on it out here.
Stomach's starting to talk. There are rations in the crate by the airlock, if I want to keep my strength up.
stages.hungry: Properly hungry now, and my hands feel slow. A ration from the cabin crate would fix that.
stages.starving: I haven't eaten in days and everything's an effort. Food, before anything else, or nothing else gets done.

stages.start: Ration packs in the cabin crate. Not exactly a feast.

first_meal.journal: First meal on Mars: a foil pouch, eaten cross-legged on the cabin deck. Tasted better than it had any right to.

stages.start: Only a couple of ration packs left in the crate. The pallets brought food. More of them out there, maybe.
I've been up a long time. A proper sleep in the sealed cabin would set me right.
stages.exhausted: I keep nodding off. Two sols without sleep. The landing seat reclines, I think.

stages.start: Did I just fall asleep standing up? On Mars? That's a new one.
Woke to a long, slow grinding somewhere out on the flats. Then nothing.

night_sound.journal: Found what made the noise in the night.

stages.start: Tracks. Six wheels, wide apart, heading out across the flats. That's what I heard in the night: one of the walkers. Worth a picture for the orbiter.
That's Walker 1, with the base's core slung under it. Fault lamp blinking, but nothing looks broken. Is it just lost? There's a seat and a screen up front.

walker_seen.journal: Found Walker 1. It wasn't broken, it was lost: its compass was way off. Gave it the sun and a few places I knew, and it walked home.

stages.start: If the cargo's all waiting by the lander, the module can have it the moment it's down.

staging.journal: Pallets 1 and 2's cargo is waiting by the lander, ready for the module.

stages.start: Walker 1's parked by the lander with the module. Now, where do I want to live? Somewhere I've walked, flat, with room to grow.

walker_home.journal: Chose where the core goes. Watched the walker lower it.

stages.start: The module came with its plans, an ice extractor among them. GAR-Y's radar can find ice near the module; core it, and drill there. The ice wall's too far to pipe in, for now. The iron needs a smelter; not yet.

module_plans.journal: Built the ice extractor where GAR-Y's core found ice. The base makes its own water now.

stages.start: First night under a real roof. It's quiet in here. I can hear my own breathing.

first_room.journal: First night in the core. A real room.

stages.start: The module's running on its own battery and a strip of roof solar. Fine by day, but it won't see out a heated night. Pallet 2's solar blanket would keep it going: it goes on the socket outside.

module_power.journal: Moved the solar blanket over to the module's socket. It holds the night now.

stages.start: A pallet, open and empty. The latches were undone from inside. Small tracks lead off from it: six wheels, close together.

cradle_empty.journal: Pallet 4 was empty when I found it, opened from the inside. Whatever was in it let itself out in the storm.
